evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A03612-001, Shuowen quotations and later variant history
evidence.text: The dictionary preserves two separate Shuowen entries: 号 is a painful cry, formed from 口 over 丂; 號 means ‘call’ and is formed from 号 and 虎. It cites later lexicons and Dunhuang usage showing the forms and readings converged, including 号 used for 號. This is lexicographic history, not independent proof of the graphs’ original construction.
evidence.title: [A03612] 號 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A03612-001, later readings and cited lexicons
evidence.text: The page reports modern Mandarin háo and hào for the converged forms. Its quotations from Yùpiān and Guǎngyùn associate 号/號 with crying, pain, calling, summoning, ordering, and posthumous title. The quotations show overlapping historical uses but do not establish a complete chronology or the first occurrence of each sense.
evidence.title: [A03612] 號 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: 金文 record for 同簋蓋
evidence.text: The record labels the displayed inscriptional form 同簋蓋, mid-Western Zhou, 集成4270. The associated regular-script label is 世, so this record is not evidence for 號; it does not verify the dossier’s claim that 號 appears on that vessel.

evidence.field: Baxter–Sagart 2014, exact rows; local file source path
evidence.text: The supplied exact rows give 丂 MC khawX, OC *C.qʰˤuʔ (‘to sob’; marked Shuōwén, no pre-Qín examples); 号 MC hawH, OC *[g]ˤaw-s (‘command, call’); and 號 MC haw, OC *[C.g]ˤaw (‘call out’), plus MC hawH, OC *Cə.[g]ˤaw-s (‘command, call’). These readings are from the local table at /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-dict/sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv; the cited project page does not expose those rows, so this item is a local cross-check, not independent external confirmation. In this reconstruction 丂 does not provide a clear sound match for 号.
evidence.title: The Baxter-Sagart reconstruction of Old Chinese

gaps: The local phonology rows were cross-checked as supplied, but the linked Baxter–Sagart project materials were not opened at row level; preserve their local provenance and notation.
Exact official Unicode Unihan records for U+53F7 and U+865F were inaccessible. The local kMandarin rows are not external verification; cite no Unihan reading claim as externally confirmed.
The selected Academia Sinica glyph record is explicitly labeled 世, not 號. It cannot support the dossier’s 同簋蓋/集成4270 claim for 號; that catalogue claim needs a correct graph-specific record.
The supplied Commons glyph file could not be inspected. Its file identity, visual content, attribution obligations, and license remain unverified; do not select it on this evidence.
No independent earliest paleographic form or oracle-bone attestation was established in this pass. MOE’s account is a dictionary history quoting Shuowen, not independent paleographic confirmation.

The retrieved sources confirm later sense overlap but do not establish dated earliest uses or a full semantic route from cry/call to title, command, sign, or number. Classical work citations alone do not date surviving witnesses.

The evidence supports the traditional Shuowen account 口 over 丂 for the separate 号 entry and 号 plus 虎 for 號. It does not establish 丂 as a phonetic component of 号; Baxter–Sagart rows supplied locally do not show an obvious sound match.

No independently recoverable historical name or pronunciation for a depicted tiger’s cry was found. The tiger-roar origin proposal remains a traditional interpretation and does not establish a whole-graph sound loan.
